metadata.note: Zanesville and Western Railway (1902-1921) and its predecessor the Columbus, Shawnee and Hocking (1890-1902, renamed Columbus, Sandusky and Hocking 1893 - one operator), as separate operator features sharing identical geometry: Columbus - Thurston (CS&H 1893 anchor only), Thurston - Zanesville main line, the Shawnee Branch Fultonham - Sayre - Corning - Drakes - Shawnee, and the Glouster and Cannelville branches; plus the modern Zanesville and Western Scenic Railroad excursions at Mount Perry. Drawn spans follow the report's drawable: fields exactly. Research report: research/branches/zanesville_and_western_railway.txt.
metadata.operator_split: Rule 4 split at the Sep/Oct 1902 CS&H -> Zanesville and Western sale (new company, own organisation per ICC): CS&H features in olive, Z&W features in plum, on identical geometry (csh-thurston-zanesville / zw-thurston-zanesville; csh-shawnee-branch-north / zw-shawnee-branch-north; csh-shawnee-branch-south / zw-shawnee-branch-south). NOT splits: the 1893 CS&H -> Columbus, Sandusky & Hocking rename and the 1895/1897 receiverships (same operator); Hocking Valley / T&OC / NYC stock control 1902-1910 (the Z&W ran its own trains to 31 Dec 1917). The 1 Jan 1922 lease to the T&OC / NYC Ohio Central Lines would be a split to the existing New York Central colour, but no passenger year after 1917 is confirmed, so no NYC feature is drawn. Columbus & Eastern (1884-1889): no confirmable passenger year, no feature. Colours: CS&H #7A8B2E, Z&W #8E3B5E and ZWSR #3D8C95 are new; a script confirmed no other company in data/ uses any of them.
not_yet_sourced: END OF PASSENGER SERVICE IS NOT DATED. zw-thurston-zanesville ends at 1917 [OPEN] (last confirmed: ICC 1917 terminal lease); zw-shawnee-branch-north and zw-shawnee-branch-south end at 1912 [OPEN] (last confirmed: 1912 shelter/station building dates). Service ran on by an unknown amount; by the Feb 1952 Official Guide every Z&W station checked is daggered freight-only. Best next sources: Hagley PRR General Chronology PDFs, 1920s-30s NYC/T&OC public timetables and Official Guides, PUCO annual reports, Zanesville and Perry County papers.

Starts also [OPEN]: zw-thurston-zanesville 1904 (1903 unconfirmed), zw-shawnee-branch-north 1905, zw-shawnee-branch-south 1909 (the 1904 Guide Z&W table may include the Shawnee branch - not checked), csh-shawnee-branch-north 1891 (1890 unconfirmed); csh-shawnee-branch-north withholds 1896-1902.

Building dates as evidence: zw-shawnee-branch-north (1905 depot, 1912 shelter) and zw-shawnee-branch-south (1909 station opening, 1912 shelters) rest on NYC valuation building dates via west2k.com; a stricter reading would reduce both to a 1912 anchor.

[ANCHOR] single-year spans: csh-columbus-thurston 1893, csh-shawnee-branch-south 1893, csh-glouster-branch 1902 (operator CS&H vs Z&W not established), csh-cannelville-branch 1893. The 1893 Official Guide (Google Books HsQsAQAAMAAJ, pp. 352-353) is known only through Steiner and Cavanaugh; checking it would firm these up.
zwsr-mount-perry ends at 2023 [OPEN]; 2013 start is forum-sourced; ride length and which bridge bounds it are not measured.
Who ran Columbus - Thurston passenger trains 1890-1892 and 1894-1902 (CS&H through cars vs T&OC after 1895) is not established.
Corporate date conflicts recorded in the report (Z&W incorporation 16 vs 17 Oct 1902; T&OC control 1903 vs Hocking Valley to 1910; T&OC/NYC merger 1938 vs 1952) change no drawn year.
omitted: [11] CS&H Redfield (Buckeye) Branch, drawable 1893 [ANCHOR]: omitted. No grade to Redfield is mapped in OSM or OHM (the router found only 0.4 mi of untagged OHM rail ending 1.2 km short of Redfield), and the length is unresolved - Fowler's indent gives about 0.5 mi from Green Hollow Junction, Cavanaugh guesses about 8 mi with mine forks, and the Redfield place node is 1.1 mi from Saltillo. Any line drawn would be a guessed stub.

[12] CS&H Sayre - Shawnee Junction (Malta) branch, drawable 1893 [ANCHOR] low confidence: omitted, as the report directs when the 1893 Guide table cannot be checked for times. Fowler gives no letters at all on route 25; the only evidence is Cavanaugh's description of the 1893 Guide listing the branch.
[14] Columbus and Eastern (1884-1889): drawable NONE - no confirmable passenger year.

Freight-only (Rule 1): San Toy Branch, Green Run branch, mine forks beyond Redfield and Cannelville (Ballous), the post-1902 East Columbus Branch, all NYC-era (1922+) Z&W track, and the 1976-1990s Conrail / Moxahala Valley / Ohio Southern Glass Rock - New Lexington operation.

properties.line: Columbus, Shawnee and Hocking: Columbus – Thurston
properties.speed_source: 1893 Official Guide (via Steiner and Cavanaugh): Columbus - Zanesville 67 mi in 150 min = about 43 km/h end to end. Taken from a described timetable, not read directly.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-30) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py. old_railway_operator=NYC is the only spelling of this road or its successors tagged in the 39.45,-83.1 to 40.05,-81.85 box (no Z&W, Zanesville & Western, T&OC, Toledo and Ohio Central, New York Central or Conrail spelling exists); OHM supplies 'Columbus and Eastern Railroad' / 'Columbus, Sandusky & Hocking Railroad' / 'Shawnee and Muskingum River Railway' and untagged grades.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 29.2 mi against about 29 mi documented (Cavanaugh: Thurston Z&W MP 28.8 from Columbus). 22.0 mi on old_railway_operator=NYC ways, 3.8 mi on untagged OpenHistoricalMap rail, 3.1 mi on untagged OSM rail, 0.2 mi PRR-tagged, 0.1 mi connectors; no straight-line legs. Waypoints within 1.3 km (Union Depot site hand-pinned at High St; Milo, Shepard, Alum Creek Jct, Doney's and Truro placed by hand from the report's street descriptions, not geocoded). Union Depot - Milo (about 2 mi) is drawn on OHM/untagged Columbus rail that runs diagonally north-east from the depot; the CS&H used Big Four track north past the State Fair Grounds to about 8th Ave, and the drawn line may cut that corner by up to 1 km - not verified against the 1934 Unification map. Alum Creek Jct - Truro follows the lifted East Columbus Branch (NYC-tagged abandoned/razed ways). Truro - Thurston is ex-Ohio Central / T&OC Columbus Branch track (CS&H trains under the Aug 1885 joint-use lease), drawn on today's live Kanawha River Railroad (West Virginia Secondary): LATER ALIGNMENT - today's track; relocations since 1893 not checked. Ends at Thurston 0.25 km from the start of csh-thurston-zanesville (separate junction legs, not joined).

segments.note: CS&H Columbus - Zanesville through route, Columbus Union Depot - Thurston section: Union Depot, Fifth Avenue, State Fair Grounds, CA&C Crossing (Milo), Shepard, Alum Creek Junction (East Columbus), Doney's (National Road), Truro, Brice, Pickerington, Basil, Baltimore, Thurston. 1893 Official Guide: 'the popular line between Columbus and Zanesville ... no change of cars', 67 mi in 150 minutes. Truro - Thurston is Ohio Central / T&OC Columbus Branch track used by the CS&H under an Aug 1885 joint-use lease, drawn here for CS&H trains only (the T&OC's own service over it is in toledo_and_ohio_central_railway.geojson). [ANCHOR] 1893 is the only proven passenger year for this piece. Service certainly ran wider in both directions, but no other year is confirmed - do not widen this anchor to look plausible, and do not delete it to tidy the map. Cavanaugh says through trains ran 'from the mid-1880s onward' and 'in the 1890s'; after the T&OC reached Truro in 1895 it is not established whether CS&H through cars kept using the Alum Creek route, and after 1902 Z&W passengers rode T&OC trains from West Broad St and changed at Thurston. Union Depot - Truro became the freight-only NYC East Columbus Branch (abandoned Truro - East Columbus by Conrail Aug 1982); its last passenger train is not dated. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

properties.line: Columbus, Shawnee and Hocking: Thurston – Zanesville
properties.speed_source: 1893 Official Guide (via Steiner and Cavanaugh): Columbus - Zanesville 67 mi in 150 min = about 43 km/h end to end. Taken from a described timetable, not read directly.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 38.4 mi against 38.6 mi (Fowler route 21, Zanesville 0.0 - Thurston 38.6) and 37.1 mi (Cavanaugh, Z&W MP 28.8 - 67.9). 33.9 mi on old_railway_operator=NYC ways (lifted grade Thurston - Glass Rock, the Zanesville and Western Scenic Railroad's leased Glass Rock - Avondale track, lifted grade east of it), 4.5 mi on untagged OpenHistoricalMap rail; no straight-line legs. Waypoints within 0.5 km except New Salem (1.5 km) and Zanesville (1.9 km - the drawn line stops at the end of the mapped Z&W grade on the west side of town, near Spangler/Brighton, and its length matches Fowler's MP 0.0). Drawn on the Z&W's own Darlington - Muskingum - South Zanesville - Spangler line, i.e. the 1890-on entry via the Zanesville Terminal, NOT the 1884-1890 Darlington - Zanesville C&MV (PRR) trackage, which falls outside any drawn year. By 1917 Z&W trains used CA&C track Spangler - Zanesville (2.21 mi) into the passenger terminal; that last stretch is not separately drawn - the line ends on the Z&W grade. Alignment changes along the line between 1890 and 1917 were not checked.

segments.note: CS&H era (Columbus, Shawnee & Hocking; renamed Columbus, Sandusky & Hocking Dec 1893 with the same initials and management; receivers 1895 and 1897-1902 - not a change of operator). Thurston, New Salem, Reservoir Park / Burket's, Thornport, Walser, Glenford, Glass Rock, Mount Perry, Cedar Grove, Fultonham, White Cottage, Elizabeth (Powell's), Lewis, Darlington, Muskingum, South Zanesville, Spangler, Zanesville. Starts 1890: Fowler's 'Burket's 1890G' former-name tag (MP 31); the line opened 1884 under the Columbus & Eastern, but no C&E-era passenger year is confirmed so nothing earlier is drawn. Ends 1902: Fowler's 'Spangler 1902G' and the 24 Sep 1902 foreclosure sale - whether the 1902 Guide predates the Z&W's Oct 1902 takeover is not established. Also confirmed: 1893 (z letters along the line; 1893 Guide through trains Columbus - Zanesville), 1895 (Reservoir Park 1895t), 1900 (Powels 1900G). 1894 Poor's: 13 passenger coaches, 3 baggage cars. Service continues under the Zanesville and Western as zw-thurston-zanesville from 1904 (1903 unconfirmed). Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler route 21 station letters and former-name tags (Burket's 1890G, z=1893G, Reservoir Park 1895t, Powels 1900G, Spangler 1902G); 1893 Official Guide via Steiner and Cavanaugh; abandonedonline for construction and sale dates. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Zanesville and Western era (incorporated 16/17 Oct 1902; 'operated by its own organization from date of acquirement until December 31, 1917' - ICC). Z&W trains ran Thurston - Zanesville; Columbus passengers changed at Thurston from T&OC trains (1904 Official Railway Guide pp. 468, 473 via Cavanaugh: Z&W No. 102 dep. Thurston 8:40 AM, connecting from T&OC No. 2 ex Columbus Broad St 7:30 AM). START 1904 is the earliest CONFIRMED Z&W year, not a known start - the Z&W took over in Oct 1902 and 1903 is unconfirmed. Passenger service confirmed to 1917 by the ICC valuation lease statement for the year ended 31 Dec 1917 (Cleveland, Akron & Cincinnati 2.21 mi Spangler - Zanesville 'included in passenger terminal use'). 1917 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped (by the Feb 1952 Official Guide every Z&W station checked is daggered freight-only, so it ended at an unknown year before 1951). Do not extend without evidence. Supporting, not used as years: NYC valuation records via west2k (Glass Rock passenger platform 1909, Glenford station extended 1916). Stock control by the Hocking Valley / T&OC (1902-03) and NYC interests (1910) did not change who ran the trains. USRA federal control 1918 - 1 Mar 1920; leased to the T&OC (NYC Ohio Central Lines) 1 Jan 1922 - any confirmed passenger year after 1921 would belong on a new New York Central-coloured feature, not here. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

segments.note: CS&H Shawnee Branch, north half: (East) Fultonham, Cannon (Garrets), Axline's, Green Hollow Junction, Saltillo, Crooksville (crossing the PRR C&MV), Reed, Tropic (Rose Farm / Deavertown), Misco, Sayre. Saltillo - Sayre was completed Oct 1890 (11.2 mi) but 1890 is not confirmed. The CS&H era ran to 1902, but 1896-1902 is not confirmed for this branch and is withheld - not a known end. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

START 1909 is the earliest CONFIRMED year, not a known start: the new Z&W Corning station, built 1908 after the CS&H depot burned, opened Aug 1909 (Zanesville Signal 20 Aug 1909 via west2k). Passenger service confirmed to 1912 by NYC valuation building dates (Buckingham passenger shelter 1912; Carrington 'passenger station made of an old car body' 1912; Hemlock station 1912) via west2k. 1912 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped (by the Feb 1952 Official Guide every Z&W station checked is daggered freight-only, so it ended at an unknown year before 1951). Do not extend without evidence. Building dates are indirect evidence; a stricter reading would reduce this to a 1912 anchor. Congo and Hemlock are daggered freight-only in the Feb 1952 Guide index. A Shawnee 'passenger station built 1906' is not attributed to a railroad (the B&O also served Shawnee) and is not used. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: Zanesville Signal 20 Aug 1909 and NYC valuation building dates as reported by west2k.com; ICC valuation summary (K&M lease); Feb 1952 Official Guide index (not an end year). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Drakes - Hamburg - Hoboken - Hartleyville - Oakdale - Superior Mine - Glouster, on the K&M-owned ex-Ohio Central 'Buckingham Branch' (built 1881-82). [ANCHOR] 1902 is the only proven passenger year for this piece. Service certainly ran wider in both directions, but no other year is confirmed - do not widen this anchor to look plausible, and do not delete it to tidy the map. Evidence: Fowler 'Hoboken 1902G'. OPERATOR UNCERTAIN: 1902 is the CS&H's last (receivership) year and the Z&W leased the line from the K&M thereafter; assigned to the CS&H because the sale was 24 Sep 1902 and the Z&W incorporated 16/17 Oct 1902. Cavanaugh says the Buckingham - Glouster track 'was shared by the Z&W and T&OC'. Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 130: 'DRAKES, OHIO-GLOUSTER, OHIO. Freight Service only.' - passengers ended at an unknown year before 1951. Matches the K&M research file, which draws nothing here. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

segments.note: Muskingum (junction on the main line about 3.7 mi from Zanesville) - Grangers - Buckeye - Brush Creek - Stovertown - Cannelville. Built 1886-87 by the Columbus & Eastern (ICC: Jan 1887; ICC measures it 'Fultonham to Cannelville' 15.70 mi, Fowler and Cavanaugh from Muskingum - drawn from Muskingum). [ANCHOR] 1893 is the only proven passenger year for this piece. Service certainly ran wider in both directions, but no other year is confirmed - do not widen this anchor to look plausible, and do not delete it to tidy the map. Evidence: Fowler z (1893G) at Grangers and Brush Creek; the 1893 Guide CS&H table includes 'branches to ... Cannelville' (Cavanaugh). Ballous, beyond Cannelville, is omitted - Fowler marks it 'z pass?'. No Z&W-era passenger evidence found; Cavanaugh's T&OC 'discontinued service' in the 1920s-30s is not stated to be passenger. Partly out of service 1926, abandoned 13 Apr 1963 (abandonedonline). Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

segments.note: Zanesville & Western Scenic Railroad (formed 2008 by the Buckeye Central Scenic / Newark, Heath & Buckeye Scenic and the Bass Run Rail Riders) - a new company, not the historic Z&W - running excursions from Mount Perry over the ex-Z&W Glass Rock Spur, leased from the State of Ohio (Glass Rock - Avondale). Rides 'between a bridge and Coopermill Road'; an extension west to SR 668 / Glass Rock is planned, not built as far as known. START 2013 is forum-sourced ('operations finally began after a 6-year hiatus', RYPN) and is the earliest confirmed year, not a known start. Event rides confirmed 2022 (Pumpkin Train), 2023 (3rd annual Train Robbery, county page) and 2024 (Hobo Camp, listing). 2023 is the last year confirmed by an official page - the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end; current (2025-26) operation is unconfirmed (zwsr.org would not load). Do not extend without evidence. Headway is a placeholder for event-day-only operation, not sourced.
